steps.text: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook pasta until al dente, rinse under cold water and drain.
In a large bowl, combine the pasta, Italian salad dressing, Caesar dressing, Parmesan cheese, red bell pepper, green bell pepper, and red onion. Mix well and serve chilled or at room temperature.

raw_recipe.headline: Italian Pasta Salad I
raw_recipe.description: This fun salad has two dressings - Italian and creamy Caesar. And with the exception of some diced bell pepper and onion, it 's all pasta.
raw_recipe.name: Italian Pasta Salad I

review.reviewBody: This is one of those recipes which allow for as much or as little liberties as you like! I personally love to jazz this Italian pasta salad up with half moon slices of pepperoni, cubed mozzarella and smoked cheddar cheeses, black olives, small pepperoncini peppers, and little grape tomatoes! It could be a meal in itself!
decreased parmesan to 1/2 cup, stirred in carrots, cucumber, 1/2 red pepper and 1/2 onion. Also added mini pepperoni and a little shredded cheddar. Now that is my kind of pasta salad!
I used Newman's Italian (full fat) and Litehouse Cesear dressing. I let the pasta sit for 6 hours before serving. My friends really like it.

It is a quick, easy recipe. But I'm not a fan of the cream sauce. I put less than required and I still didn't really like it. But maybe it's just me. I also sauted the green peppers, red peppers, and onions with basil and oregano. Adds alittle flavor to the veggies. Fairly certain that pieces of cooked chicken would taste wonderful as well. Also I did not add all the cheese to the mix. I just sprinkled a little on the top and mixed it in. But it was good.

Fantastic Pasta Salad!
I am picky about pasta salad: I don't like it when they are too oily and vinegar-y, and I don't like it when they are too mayonaise-y. This recipe is a perfect balance with the Italian and Caesar dressings. 
I read the reviews, and included yellow & orange bell peppers with the red & green (used 1/2 of each color), and a cup of cubed mozzarella. It was a big hit and everyone had seconds! I will definitely be saving this recipe for the future.

It's a super simple and delicious pasta salad. I loved it because it's so easy to add to it and it completely changes the taste. I swapped the onion for red onion, added lots of fresh dill and some crumbled feta. Delicious! Also because the dressing is all pre-made I always buy the expensive refrigerated stuff - you can really taste the difference.

I've made this wonderful tasty recipe a few times! I've added provolone chunks, pepperoni, zucchini chunks, basil, cherry tomatoes, and sometimes ham chunks instead of the pepperoni, to the existing recipe. It really looks pretty and it's the first salad to disappear! Big crowd pleaser!
Absolutely LOVE this pasta salad. I use the tri-color pasta and it looks beautiful. I also add chopped cucumbers. My whole family LOVES it!!

This is the first recipe I ever tried when I discovered All Recipes, so I’ve been making it for years. I use Wish Bone’s Creamy Caesar Dressing, and their Zesty Robusto Italian Dressing. I also add some halved cherry tomatoes. It is the most requested pasta I make. Delicious!

This recipe was a delicious spin on the traditional Italian pasta salad with Italian dressing. The dressing combination makes this pasta salad scrumptious. To make it a bit healthier I used yogurt based Caesar dressing, found in the produce section called Caesar Parmigiano, that was 45 calories and 2.5 grams fat per 2 tbsps. It went perfect with the brand name Lite House Italian dressing with similar nutrition information I used. I would highly recommend the Caesar dressing I used as full calorie tasting alternative to the actual full calorie versions, in fact it might be a bit tastier. At first I used the dressings in proportions given in the recipe and it was delicious, but to make it creamier for my tastes I ended up using about 15% more Caesar then Italian. I’m not a big fan of bell peppers, so I used my preference of veggies including broccoli, cucumber, cauliflower, red onion, and black olives which were terrific. Next time I might add sugar snap peas. I brought some to share with my co-workers and they couldn’t get enough of this salad. This recipe is a great non-run-of-the-mill pasta salad base that you can dress up with your favorite veggies and add-ins. I highly recommend it as a fantastic make ahead lunch for work or to bring to a summer cook out, you won’t be disappointed!

I really liked this recipe because it is super easy and has fewer steps than many other pasta salad recipes. I tweaked it a bit by using what I had on hand. I had garden rotini pasta and used 8 oz. I used a frozen steam-in-bag mixture of broccoli, carrots and cauliflower (cooked per directions). I then added 1/4 cup chopped onion and 1/2 jar of roasted red pepper. Lastly I added 1/2 cup each of the following: Italian salad dressing, light Caesar salad dressing and Parmesan cheese. This is an easy simple recipe that can be prepared with what you have in the pantry. I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 because it is heavy on the dressing. Next time I would use less. I've posted a picture - it looks great and would be nice for a summer potluck dinner.
It was good and simple to make. I will definitely make it again.
I’ve made it several times sometimes I add fresh tomatoes and cucumbers and even green onion. It’s always good.
Pretty good. May add cherry tomatoes and cucumbers next time.
My husband LOVES this recipe!
Very nice!
Delicious! I chopped up whatever veggies I had and added olives.
This is a great pasta salad recipe! Thank you for sharing
I added the ingredients it says. Not a full cup in dressings. Yeah made extra pasta 16 oz didnt seem enough.
Added mini pepperoni and small mild cheddar cubes, it was great and exactly what I was looking for. I would definitely make it again.
